transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-30
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Miles Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood), Laura Kim (Zenvera Head of ML), Rajesh Narayan (Platform Lead), Evelyn Shore (SRE), Tom Higgins (Procurement)

Summary:
- Scope POC traffic/playbook to validate latency SLOs and cost envelope for Zenvera Health conversational assistants.
- Agree on traffic replay artifact, benchmark plan, and success criteria (latency quantiles, throughput, error budget).
- Discussed hosted vs private, KV cache behavior, and data residency / KMS requirements.

Topics covered:
- Workload portrait (QPS, concurrency, diurnal bursts)
- Input/output token distributions and tail token lengths
- Benchmark design: steady-state vs burst playback, warm vs cold KV cache runs
- Success criteria: 95th/99th latency gates, error rate, cost per 1M tokens target
- Timeline and next steps for artifact delivery and bench runs

References/Links mentioned:
- Benchmark plan (drive link): https://drive.example.com/zenvera-poc-plan
- Security pack (SOC2 + ISO): https://redwood.example.com/security/zenvera
- Replay instruction doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/poc-replay

Action items recap in call:
- Priya to craft benchmark spreadsheet with QPS/concurrency matrix and token-length buckets (will include cold/warm cache runs).
- Rajesh to provide 48h anonymized traffic + top-1k prompts.
- Miles to schedule bench slot and circulate security/architecture docs.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Miles Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Miles from Redwood, i'll hand it over quick to priya to run the bench plan and then we'll get into questions.
[00:37] Priya Rao: yeah hi all, thanks. um quick agenda — want to align on traffic shape, success gates, and artifacts we need. Laura, can you kick off with a quick portrait of what your assistant sees?
[02:05] Laura Kim: sure — so our core assistant has two modes, triage chat for intake which is short (usually 20–80 input tokens, 10–40 out), and then clinical draft that is much longer — 400 to 1,200 tokens out sometimes, inputs of 150–600 tokens. average QPS today is low, 0.6 globally, but we have big bursts in morning windows where concurrency spikes to ~120. um, so tail matters.
[05:12] Rajesh Narayan: to add, our pattern is very nonstationary — weekdays 9am to 11am heavy, also monthly batch jobs that cause a spike when we bootstrap context for long threads. we can export 48 hours that show this.
[07:20] Priya Rao: ok helpful — when you say spike to 120 concurrency, is that user sessions or inflight requests?
[07:38] Laura Kim: inflight requests, yeah, roughly. some of that is websocket session multiplexing from mobile app.
[09:02] Daniel Ortiz: just to set expectations, for long outputs (400+ tokens) batching behavior differs, we'll get higher throughput but tail latency is sensitive to KV cache warm state and sequence length. also quantization choices affect output quality.
[12:01] Evelyn Shore: can you explain the KV cache bit — we care about warm vs cold runs because our e2e SLA is 95th < 450ms for 256-token responses, but we also see 99th tails that blow up during spikes.
[13:22] Priya Rao: yeah so KV cache (prefix cache) keeps the activations for repeated context, so warm-cache can reduce per-token compute significantly. but with long context windows (you mentioned 1,200 tokens) cold cache runs will be expensive and increase latency. for the bench we recommend three scenarios: 1) cold start, 2) warm steady-state, 3) burst overlay on warm.
[15:40] Laura Kim: that sounds good. what's realistic to capture in replay, do you need the raw messages or tokenized artifacts?
[16:12] Miles Chen: tokenized is ideal but raw is fine — we have a tokenizer pipeline, but if you can provide a sample of top-1k prompts that'll let us compute realistic input token distributions.
[17:55] Tom Higgins: quick procurement question — private deployment costs vs hosted, and can we toggle encryption with customer KMS? we need pricing to compare total cost.
[18:32] Miles Chen: yes, private supports KMS/HSM integrations, and we'll include a cost estimate in the bench playbook. hosted can be faster to stand up but private gives control over keys and network egress.
[19:45] Rajesh Narayan: also curious about routing/fallback — if a heavy model is down can you route to a smaller quantized variant gracefully?
[20:10] Priya Rao: absolutely — smart routing & automatic fallback is part of the runtime, we can set rollout policies for canary or fallback to a lower-cost quantized model with slightly higher error rate. we'll include fallback scenarios in the benchmark.
[21:40] Laura Kim: success criteria — we want to validate three gates: (A) 95th latency under baseline QPS (0.6) for 256-token outputs < 450ms, (B) 99th under 2x baseline (1.2 QPS) with burst overlay (concurrency 120) < 900ms, (C) error rate < 0.2% and cost per 1M tokens under $X — we need Redwood to provide a cost delta for quantized runs.
[24:05] Priya Rao: noted. we'll define exact token buckets and cost calc in spreadsheet. for the bursts we recommend replaying your 10 highest-impact minutes as a stress overlay on steady-state to replicate cache pressure.
[26:32] Daniel Ortiz: for benchmarking methodology, we'll run: warm runs for 30 minutes to stabilize cache, then three repeated cold-start runs, then two burst replays. we'll capture per-token CPU/GPU utilization, concurrency histogram, and tail latencies.
[30:15] Rajesh Narayan: one open item — data residency: some of our records are EU-resident. can you isolate inference in eu-west region and ensure no cross-region caching?
[31:02] Miles Chen: yes, region pinning and routing policies can be set; private deployment gives additional guarantees. we'll note isolation in the security doc.
[33:40] Evelyn Shore: on SOC2 and audit logs — can we get redwood's audit retention policy and integration points with our SIEM?
[34:10] Miles Chen: yes, we'll share SOC2 summary and syslog/trace integration details. link in chat after call.
[36:20] Laura Kim: about sample size — do you think 48 hours enough to capture monthly batch spikes?
[36:45] Priya Rao: 48 hours usually shows diurnal patterns; to capture monthly batch you can supply synthetic event that simulates the bootstrap. we can seed traffic replay with that synthetic spike.
[38:50] Tom Higgins: procurement — what's typical POC timeline? we need internal signoffs end of next week.
[39:10] Miles Chen: typical POC: artifact exchange (this week), bench setup (week of 2027-05-03), bench runs (2027-05-06 to 2027-05-07), results review (2027-05-10). flexible but we can compress.
[41:00] Rajesh Narayan: ok. on artifact privacy — can Redwood run the benchmarks in our account (private) or do you need to ingest data to Redwood-hosted test cluster?
[41:28] Priya Rao: we can run both: option A is run in your VPC with a private control plane (we'll provide deployment steps), option B is a hosted bench but we only use anonymized tokenized payloads. we'll list tradeoffs in the plan.
[43:05] Daniel Ortiz: small note — when you export tokens, include conversation IDs so we can preserve context-length distributions; if that's sensitive you can hash IDs.
[44:33] Laura Kim: will do. one more question — how do you measure cost per 1M tokens with batching?
[45:02] Priya Rao: we measure effective tokens billed plus infra run time; batching reduces per-token cost but increases effective tail for small requests. the spreadsheet will show tokenized cost model across quantization and batch sizes.
[46:50] Miles Chen: also we'll capture cold cache penalty as an explicit line item — this is important for monthly cold boot scenarios.
[48:20] Evelyn Shore: any red flags we should be aware of? our data has many medical abbreviations, will that affect tokenization and perf?
[48:46] Priya Rao: sometimes domain-specific token distributions increase sequence length due to rare tokens, we'll check token histograms and recommend token-merging or vocab adapt if needed.
[50:20] Laura Kim: ok, to summarize — we will share traffic, Redwood will run warm/cold/burst bench, measure 95/99 latencies and cost, and then reconvene.
[51:10] Tom Higgins: procurement needs a short summary doc for finance — can you send estimated POC cost?
[51:35] Miles Chen: yes. I'll include a rough POC estimate and a breakdown: bench infra + engineering time + optional private deployment prep.
[53:12] Rajesh Narayan: last ask — can you include a quick runbook for toggling fallback models in case a larger model fails?
[53:40] Daniel Ortiz: yes, we'll add a step-by-step runbook and an example config for routes and fallbacks.
[55:05] Miles Chen: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and links. next touchpoint — bench kickoff early next week, i'll send times.
[55:40] Laura Kim: thanks all. bye.

End of transcript.
